title: AI chip designer Aurora Silicon raises $410 million in Series D round
author: Staff and wire reports
text:
Aurora Silicon raises $410 million in a Series D funding round led by Calder Peak Capital, the AI chip designer said on Tuesday, a deal that values the company at about $3.1 billion.

The Texas-based startup, which designs low-power accelerators for running trained models rather than training them, said the capital will pay for volume production of its A9 inference chip and roughly double its engineering headcount over the next 18 months.

Northgate Ventures and Halcyon Capital, both existing investors, also took part. Aurora Silicon has secured about $720 million from investors since its founding in 2021.

"Inference is where the money is going to be spent for the rest of the decade," co-founder Lena Varga said. "Customers want chips that cut their cost per token, not just chips that top a benchmark."

A9 samples are being tested by three unnamed cloud providers, according to the company, with first production shipments expected in mid-2027.
